name: contested-br-cut-mid-stream
description: A br stream cut at three quarters of its length decodes cleanly to a prefix: the reference decoder cannot see the cut.
grounding: The salvage rule requires the decoder to report the cut, and for br the reference decoder does not: andybalholm/brotli returns a clean EOF on a stream truncated mid-block, so partial output is indistinguishable from a complete body. Recorded as observed rather than promoted to the salvage rule.

contested.question: A truncated br stream decodes silently to a prefix in the reference implementation — the exact silent-truncation failure the salvage rule exists to make loud for gzip and zstd. Does the Rust consumer's brotli decoder report the cut?
contested.decision: Record the reference's observed behavior. br truncation goes unreported until a decoder that can see the cut exists on both sides; the case then flips to outcome salvaged and joins the per-coding salvage rules.
contested.open: Rust consumer: report what your brotli decoder does with this input. If it errors or reports truncation, this is a genuine cross-language divergence to resolve in the reference (as contested-empty-body-under-zstd was, PCC-1134).
contested.suspected_bug: Upstream limitation, not a policy choice: the Go reader maps input-exhausted-mid-block to io.EOF once any output was produced (only a cut before the first byte of output surfaces as unexpected EOF).

notes: PCC-1276. A cut early enough to produce no output does error (unexpected EOF, nothing produced), which lands in the salvage-refused-when-nothing-produced rule's class; this case pins the mid-stream cut, which does not.
